options.B: Black
options.C: Red
options.D: Green

explanation: Patients who have sadly passed away or have injuries incompatible with life are tagged black (expectant) so resources can go to those who can be saved.

question: When working in emergency healthcare, what does the acronym MHPSS stand for?

options.A: Medical Health and Physical Social Services
options.B: Managed Hospital Patient Safety Systems
options.C: Multidisciplinary Healthcare Professional Support Staff
options.D: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support

explanation: You got this! MHPSS stands for Mental Health and Psychosocial Support. It covers both the emotional and social help people need during crises.

question: What does evaluating a menu mean in quality improvement?

options.A: A strict punishment system for kitchen staff who make cooking errors
options.B: A continuous process of gathering feedback and adjusting meals to meet client needs
options.C: A one-time inspection that happens only when the kitchen first opens
options.D: A method to permanently stop changing the food served in the ward

explanation: It's all about checking in regularly, listening to patient feedback, and tweaking the menu so everyone is well-fed and happy.

question: Which data quality rule means we should document care right after giving it?

options.A: Completeness
options.B: Consistency
options.C: Timeliness
options.D: Accessibility

explanation: Timeliness means writing things down promptly so the chart always reflects what is happening with the patient right now.

question: Why is it important to regularly calibrate hospital research equipment?

options.A: To prevent measurement errors that ruin data accuracy
options.B: To shorten the time required for patient interviews
options.C: To make the equipment look newer to inspectors
options.D: To ensure patients pay lower hospital bills

explanation: Exactly right! If our tools aren't accurate, our data won't be either. Calibration keeps our numbers honest.

question: Which statement best describes the role of nurse managers when using scheduling software?

options.A: They have no control over the roster once the computer generates it
options.B: They are only responsible for entering patient billing data into the system
options.C: They stop working night shifts completely because software handles them
options.D: They must still review and adjust schedules for human factors and emergencies

explanation: Software assists with the math, but nurse managers must use clinical judgment for unexpected personal situations. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is a major risk when electronic health record systems experience sudden downtime?

options.A: All medication pumps stop working simultaneously
options.B: Staff must revert to paper charting, which can increase transcription errors
options.C: Hospital doors automatically lock to prevent patient entry
options.D: Patient vital signs automatically delete themselves from memory

explanation: System downtime forces a return to manual paper records, raising the chance of mistakes during handovers and order transcription. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the medical term for the condition caused by a dangerous buildup of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain?

options.A: Microcephaly
options.B: Hydrocephalus
options.C: Encephalitis
options.D: Meningitis

explanation: You're doing amazing! 'Hydrocephalus' literally means 'water on the brain,' referring to trapped fluid swelling up the ventricles.

question: Why are peer champions so valuable for sustaining long-term changes in a nursing unit?

options.A: They write all the hospital policies and clinical guidelines.
options.B: They handle the payroll and administrative duties for the ward.
options.C: They model the new behaviors and encourage their colleagues.
options.D: They are responsible for punishing staff who refuse to comply.

explanation: Peer champions lead by example on the floor, making it much easier for other nurses to adopt new ways with confidence.

question: A rural health clinic receives a dedicated increase in operational funding. What improvement should the nurse expect to see first?

options.A: A surplus of specialized neurosurgeons
options.B: Decreased need for community health education
options.C: Availability of open-heart surgery equipment
options.D: Reliable vaccine storage and basic medical supplies

explanation: Primary health care priorities focus on basic infrastructure, vaccines, and essential medications rather than highly specialized surgical gear. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h3)

question: Which feature is most characteristic of a quantitative research study?

options.A: Statistical analysis and measurement
options.B: Detailed personal stories and interviews
options.C: Focus only on historical events
options.D: Absence of any numerical data

explanation: Quantitative research deals with numbers, variables, and measurable outcomes to test hypotheses. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is a standard way to check if a community health team is doing a good job?

options.A: Number of desks in the clinic
options.B: Color of the patient charts
options.C: Age of the supervising doctor
options.D: Hospital readmission rates

explanation: You've got it! Lower readmission rates usually mean the community team is doing a stellar job keeping people well at home.

question: When summarizing key results for a study on preventing pressure sores, what belongs right at the start?

options.A: Detailed instructions on how to use turning sheets
options.B: A complete list of every patient's medical history
options.C: Raw survey responses from all participating nurses
options.D: The main answer to the primary research question

explanation: You're crushing it! Always address the main question first so your reader immediately knows what the study found.

question: Why do hospitals enforce strict double-key storage and witness counts for narcotics?

options.A: To prevent drug diversion and control abuse risks
options.B: To make medication administration take longer for nurses
options.C: To test whether the patient actually needs pain relief
options.D: To ensure the pharmaceutical company makes more profit

explanation: Strict counting and witness rules protect controlled substances from theft, misuse, or illegal diversion. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why is pushing down on top of the mother's bump (fundal pressure) a big no-no during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: It stops the placenta from delivering after the baby
options.B: It makes the baby turn around into a breech position
options.C: It causes the mother's blood pressure to drop too low
options.D: It can cause the trapped shoulder to wedge tighter and rupture the uterus

explanation: Pushing from above only jams the shoulder harder against the bone. Avoid fundal pressure completely in shoulder dystocia!

question: What happens to the lower back curve of the spine when you slouch forward for a long time?

options.A: It locks into a permanently curved position
options.B: It stops the flow of cerebrospinal fluid completely
options.C: It becomes stronger and more flexible
options.D: It flattens and over stretches supporting ligaments

explanation: Exactly. Slouching flattens your natural lower back curve, putting a lot of unnecessary strain on the supporting soft tissues. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge when trying to provide mental health care in primary clinics?

options.A: Severe shortage of trained psychiatric personnel
options.B: Strong cultural stigma surrounding mental illness
options.C: Inadequate funding for mental health services
options.D: Excessive availability of specialized psychiatrists in rural villages

explanation: You got it! Rural villages actually face a massive shortage of psychiatrists, so having 'too many' of them is definitely not a barrier!

question: Which sign tells a nurse that a local skin infection is starting to spread through the whole body?

options.A: Elevated body temperature and abnormal white blood cell counts
options.B: A decrease in the patient's daily fluid intake and urine output
options.C: Changes in the patient's preference for sweet or salty foods
options.D: The patient's ability to walk unassisted down the hospital hallway

explanation: Fever (elevated temperature) and high white blood cell counts are classic systemic red flags telling you the infection is going body-wide.

question: What official list guides healthcare workers on which medicines are approved for public health facilities?

options.A: Essential Medicines List
options.B: Standard Nursing Care Plan
options.C: Global Import Tariff Book
options.D: Private Pharmacy Catalog

explanation: Well done! The Essential Medicines List (EML) contains the carefully selected drugs needed to meet the priority healthcare needs of the community.

question: Why might a family caregiver act defensive when you ask them questions?

options.A: They are trained professional nurses themselves
options.B: Caregiver fatigue and stress can make them sensitive
options.C: Hospital rules require them to act defensively
options.D: They want to hide the patient's medical history on purpose

explanation: Caring for a sick loved one 24/7 is exhausting. If a caregiver seems defensive, they are likely just tired and overwhelmed—a little empathy goes a long way!

question: What is the best long-term way to prevent ascariasis outbreaks in communities?

options.A: Administering yearly vaccinations to all newborns
options.B: Improving sanitation infrastructure and health education
options.C: Spraying chemical pesticides on all residential soil
options.D: Isolating infected individuals in quarantine wards

explanation: Stopping the cycle comes down to the basics: clean water, proper toilets, handwashing, and community health education.

question: Where is the safest place to throw away a used injection needle immediately after giving an injection?

options.A: In an open cardboard box on the desk
options.B: In the general sink drain for washing
options.C: In a regular black plastic trash bag
options.D: In a puncture-proof safety box

explanation: Well done! Sharps boxes protect you and your colleagues from accidental needle-prick injuries.

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: Why is preventing hypothermia so important when stabilizing a trauma victim?

options.A: Standard rescue stretchers only function properly in warm weather
options.B: Hypothermia causes patients to become overly aggressive with staff
options.C: Warm patients require fewer intravenous fluids during transport
options.D: Cold exposure worsens blood clotting problems and increases mortality

explanation: You're doing awesome. Trauma patients lose body heat fast, and cold temperatures stop blood from clotting properly, making bleeding much harder to control.

question: What is the main function of an early warning system in a disaster context?

options.A: Calculating the financial cost of destroyed property
options.B: Treating injuries after a building collapses
options.C: Detecting threats early before they cause widespread harm
options.D: Punishing individuals who ignore safety rules

explanation: Early warning systems use technology and data to spot danger ahead of time so people can prepare and evacuate. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T2#GNS315_U5_T2_h3)

question: A patient arrives in the emergency unit after a severe motorcycle crash. According to the ABCDE rule, what should the nurse check first?

options.A: Blood pressure
options.B: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.C: Airway patency
options.D: Hidden skin wounds

explanation: Airway is always the top priority in the ABCDE approach because an obstructed airway causes death faster than anything else. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T2#GNS315_U2_T2_h2)

question: In a research study, what do we call the 'independent variable'?

options.A: The total number of patients who refused to participate
options.B: The intervention or cause manipulated by the researcher
options.C: The final outcome measured at the end of the project
options.D: The random error that occurs during data collection

explanation: You got it! The independent variable is the active ingredient or change that the researcher introduces to see what happens.

question: A charge nurse expects more malaria cases during the rainy season and adds extra staff early. What management function is this?

options.A: Budgeting
options.B: Controlling
options.C: Planning
options.D: Delegating

explanation: Spotting future needs ahead of time and getting ready for them is the definition of planning. You're thinking like a true nurse leader!

question: Which level of health care serves as the first point of contact for a rural community?

options.A: Secondary Health Care
options.B: Private specialist clinics
options.C: Primary Health Care
options.D: Tertiary Health Care

explanation: Primary health centers are built right inside communities to handle everyday health needs first. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why does adaptive immunity fight off a familiar germ much faster and stronger the second time around?

options.A: Because innate barriers disappear over time
options.B: Because the germ becomes weaker inside the body
options.C: Because it creates immunological memory
options.D: Because white blood cells multiply without stopping

explanation: Spot on! Your adaptive immune system keeps memory cells from past infections so it can launch a fast, targeted attack if the germ returns.

question: What does it mean when a nurse decides to 'cluster care' during a shift?

options.A: Grouping all patients with the same diagnosis in one bay
options.B: Doing several care tasks during one room visit to save time
options.C: Handing over multiple patients to a colleague all at once
options.D: Writing all patient charts at the very end of the shift

explanation: Spot on! Clustering care is a smart student trick: instead of walking in and out all day, you combine vitals, meds, and repositioning into one smooth bedside visit.

question: Which contraceptive method offers protection against both unintended pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Lactational amenorrhea method
options.B: Progestin-only injectable pills
options.C: Male and female condoms
options.D: Combined oral contraceptive pills

explanation: Condoms act as physical barriers that prevent the exchange of body fluids, protecting against both pregnancy and infections. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h7)

question: Why do vaguely worded living wills cause problems for the healthcare team?

options.A: Because nurses are not legally allowed to read handwritten documents
options.B: Because insurance companies refuse to pay for vague medical forms
options.C: Because hospitals require notarized stamps on every single page
options.D: Because terms like 'heroic measures' can mean different things to different people

explanation: Vague phrases create ambiguity, leaving nurses and physicians unsure of whether the patient intended to refuse specific interventions like intubation or IV fluids. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T7#GNS221_U4_T7_h6)

question: If a line graph has multiple lines on it, what is the purpose of the legend?

options.A: To show the maximum possible score on the vertical axis
options.B: To explain the mathematical formula used to calculate the average
options.C: To state the name of the hospital where the research took place
options.D: To identify which color or pattern belongs to each specific variable

explanation: Spot on! The legend acts like a key, helping you figure out which line represents which group without guessing.

question: What must be obtained from participants before data collection begins?

options.A: Proof of employment
options.B: A financial deposit
options.C: Physician resignation
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Participants must voluntarily agree to take part after fully understanding what the study involves. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h5)

question: During normal internal rotation, which way does the back of the baby's head (occiput) usually turn?

options.A: Toward the maternal pubic symphysis
options.B: Toward the hollow of the sacrum
options.C: Toward the right lateral pelvic wall
options.D: Toward the left maternal iliac crest

explanation: Spot on! The occiput rotates forward toward the pubic bone so it can easily slip out of the birth canal.

question: What is the very first thing you put on when wearing a full set of PPE?

options.A: Put on protective eyewear
options.B: Put on the surgical mask
options.C: Put on the isolation gown
options.D: Put on non-sterile gloves

explanation: That's correct! Always start with your gown, tying it securely to cover your uniform first. Your gloves always go on last, right over the gown sleeves.

question: What is the main role of the mucociliary escalator in the nasal cavity?

options.A: To secrete specialized enzymes that dissolve food odors
options.B: To pump fresh oxygen directly into the pulmonary capillaries
options.C: To cool down overheated air before it enters the trachea
options.D: To transport trapped debris toward the throat for removal

explanation: Beating cilia move the sticky mucus layer backward so dust and bacteria are safely swallowed rather than entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which service is provided in a Comprehensive EmONC (CEmONC) facility that is NOT part of a basic facility?

options.A: Basic neonatal resuscitation training
options.B: Provision of iron and folic acid supplements
options.C: Blood transfusions and caesarean sections
options.D: Administration of routine tetanus vaccines

explanation: Major surgeries like caesarean sections and blood banking are what upgrade a facility from basic to comprehensive EmONC. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT permitted when managing an emergency patient who lacks capacity?

options.A: Refusing treatment based solely on the patient's unpaid hospital bills
options.B: Providing emergency life-saving interventions without a signed form
options.C: Inserting an intravenous line to administer emergency fluids
options.D: Performing a rapid head-to-toe physical examination for injuries

explanation: Emergency laws forbid turning away patients with urgent medical conditions based on their financial status or inability to pay. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of these tasks is the main job of the scrub nurse during an operation?

options.A: Positioning the operating table and adjusting surgical lights
options.B: Tracking sponge counts and handing instruments to the surgeon
options.C: Managing patient billing and specimen transport logistics
options.D: Completing the electronic health record and nursing notes

explanation: The scrub nurse stays sterile right at the field, passing tools smoothly and keeping a careful count of sponges and instruments.

question: How does trial leave differ mainly from occasional leave?

options.A: Trial leave is only given to patients who refuse oral medications
options.B: Trial leave lasts much longer, often weeks or months, acting as a test for discharge
options.C: Trial leave requires the patient to stay inside a locked community center
options.D: Trial leave completely severs the patient's connection to the hospital

explanation: Trial leave is an extended test run lasting weeks or months to see if the patient is truly ready to head home permanently.

question: Which of the following is NOT a consequence of poor specimen collection technique?

options.A: Prescription of incorrect antibiotics
options.B: Need for painful repeat sample collection
options.C: Immediate cure of the bacterial infection
options.D: Inaccurate laboratory test results

explanation: Bad collection leads to wrong results and wrong drugs, which makes the infection drag on—it definitely won't cure it!

question: As a community health nurse, you notice several villagers showing signs of fever and yellow eyes. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Report the cluster to local public health authorities for investigation
options.B: Distribute mosquito repellent creams without informing the government
options.C: Advise villagers to wait two weeks to see if symptoms disappear
options.D: Close down all local markets and schools in the affected region

explanation: You're a star! Always report unusual clusters of disease right away so public health teams can step in and protect the whole community. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h8)

question: What is the main goal of tele-nursing?

options.A: Replacing all physical hospitals with apps
options.B: Manufacturing digital medical equipment
options.C: Diagnosing diseases without a doctor
options.D: Delivering nursing care using technology

explanation: Spot on! Tele-nursing simply means using tools like phones and video links to care for patients from a distance.

question: When is the best time to bring in palliative care for a patient diagnosed with lymphoma?

options.A: Only during the final 24 hours of life
options.B: Alongside regular curative treatment right from the start
options.C: Only when the patient asks for hospice
options.D: After all chemotherapy options have failed

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for end-of-life; it's about comfort and symptom relief, and it works best when started early alongside cancer treatment!

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving a patient a new biological medication?

options.A: Ensuring the medication is stored in direct sunlight at room temperature
options.B: Crushing the vial contents into water for oral intake
options.C: Assuming all biological products are completely safe from side effects
options.D: Watching the patient closely for any signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Because biological and animal-based drugs carry a higher risk of triggering the immune system, keeping a close eye on your patient is a must.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical focus of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Reframing unhelpful beliefs regarding sexuality
options.B: Reducing anxiety related to sexual performance
options.C: Surgical reconstruction of the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: Challenging negative thoughts about body image

explanation: Spot on! CBT is all about thoughts, feelings, and behaviors—surgeries are definitely left for surgical specialists!

question: What is the main purpose of an assisted living facility?

options.A: Serving as a permanent substitute for acute hospital stays
options.B: Housing only individuals with severe mental health disorders
options.C: Providing support for daily tasks while keeping independence
options.D: Offering around-the-clock intensive medical and surgical care

explanation: Assisted living is designed for people who need some help with daily living but do not require heavy nursing care, allowing them to remain as independent as possible. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which observational tool is best used to grade the quality or frequency of a specific behavior?

options.A: Simple checklist
options.B: Consent form
options.C: Rating scale
options.D: Archival record

explanation: Think of a rating scale as a grading tool. It lets you measure the degree or quality of an action, rather than just noting if it happened or not.

question: Why is it smart to involve local community leaders when planning health teaching strategies?

options.A: They pay the salaries of community health extension workers
options.B: Their backing helps increase local acceptance of the health message
options.C: National law requires them to sign off on nursing shift rosters
options.D: They are qualified to prescribe prescription drugs during emergencies

explanation: You got it! Community leaders are trusted figures. When they support a cause, residents are much more willing to listen and join in.

question: Why can low levels of the brain chemical GABA lead to feeling more anxious?

options.A: GABA is responsible for speeding up heart rate during exercise.
options.B: GABA normally dampens neural activity, so a shortage leaves the brain overactive.
options.C: GABA produces the adrenaline needed to fight off physical infections.
options.D: GABA blocks serotonin from reaching the receptors in the brain.

explanation: GABA is your brain's natural chill pill! When you are short on it, your nerve cells keep firing away unchecked, leaving you feeling high-strung.

question: What is the main danger of dumping and burning medical waste out in the open?

options.A: It pollutes the air and spreads dangerous pathogens into soil and water
options.B: It wastes valuable electrical energy that the hospital could have used
options.C: It makes the municipal waste collectors take much longer to finish routes
options.D: It causes local hospital linen to become stained with dark soot

explanation: Open burning creates toxic smoke, and dumping waste outside leaves germs out in the open where they can infect people and water sources.

question: Which germ is the main cause of tuberculosis (TB)?

options.A: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
options.D: Bordetella pertussis

explanation: TB is caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It loves to settle in the lungs! You'll get this easily with practice.

question: If a young child has a low height-for-age, what does this usually tell us?

options.A: Temporary fluid retention
options.B: Normal genetic short stature
options.C: Chronic or long-term malnutrition
options.D: Sudden weight loss from diarrhea

explanation: Height takes time to change, so a low height-for-age points to long-term nutritional challenges or repeated illnesses over time.

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical environmental challenge for home health nurses?

options.A: Navigating unfamiliar neighborhoods during community visits
options.B: Cluttered walkways and poor lighting inside private residences
options.C: Managing biohazardous waste disposal without hospital utility rooms
options.D: Guaranteed 24-hour security guards stationed outside the front door

explanation: Home care nurses do not have personal security guards stationed at every home visit; environmental risks are often unpredictable. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is a key role of the community nurse when a family needs financial or social help?

options.A: Connecting and referring them to available local support systems
options.B: Taking legal custody of their children
options.C: Paying their debts using your own clinic allowance
options.D: Telling them to stay away from government welfare programs

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you act as a bridge by linking families to community groups, NGOs, and welfare programs that can help them.

question: What is the primary function of the sarcoplasmic reticulum inside a muscle fiber?

options.A: Anchoring the muscle to nearby bone tissue
options.B: Transmitting nerve impulses along the surface
options.C: Producing ATP through aerobic respiration
options.D: Storing and releasing calcium ions

explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum holds calcium ions until an electrical impulse triggers their release to start contraction. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T9#GNS121_U3_T9_h3)

question: How should you communicate updates to the worried family of a critically ill patient?

options.A: Giving all information through a written notebook only
options.B: Speaking very quickly so they do not interrupt
options.C: Using clear, simple language without heavy medical jargon
options.D: Refusing to answer questions until visiting hours end

explanation: Families under stress need kindness and clarity. Dropping heavy medical terms just confuses them—keep it simple and reassuring!

question: Why does stopping breastfeeding early increase a baby's chance of getting diarrhoea?

options.A: It stops the liver from storing adequate iron reserves
options.B: It forces the infant to produce too much stomach acid
options.C: It causes immediate permanent damage to the pancreas
options.D: It removes protective maternal antibodies that guard the infant gut

explanation: Breast milk is liquid gold for babies! It carries special antibodies that shield their delicate digestive system from germs while their own immune system is still growing.

question: Why do clinics with flexible operating hours attract more adolescent clients?

options.A: Medical supplies are cheaper to buy at night
options.B: Government regulations require 24-hour youth attendance
options.C: Teenagers can visit without missing school classes or exams
options.D: Staff members prefer working late evening hours

explanation: Flexible schedules remove major roadblocks, making it easy for students to take care of their health without disrupting their studies.

question: What is one exciting benefit expected from future voice-activated documentation tools?

options.A: Allowing nurses to speak clinical notes while performing procedures
options.B: Replacing the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.C: Automatically bathing patients using robotic spray systems
options.D: Eliminating all hospital noise during the night shift

explanation: Brilliant! Voice tech aims to save us time by letting us dictate our notes hands-free while we work.

question: What do we call the entire group of people a researcher actually wants to study?

options.A: Population
options.B: Parameter
options.C: Variable
options.D: Sample

explanation: That's correct! The 'population' is the total group you are interested in—like all diabetic patients in Lagos State. Keep up the great flow!

question: A patient works in a chemical factory and is worried about fertility. Which background detail helps you catch this risk?

options.A: Religious affiliation
options.B: Home address
options.C: Occupation
options.D: Marital status

explanation: Spot on! Knowing what a patient does for a living helps you check if they are exposed to workplace toxins or heavy physical stress that could affect their reproductive health.

question: Why is double-checking (validating) your data such an important step in assessment?

options.A: It is required by law to be completed within fifteen minutes of admission
options.B: It allows the nurse to delegate all future care tasks to unlicensed staff
options.C: It ensures your information is correct before you make clinical choices
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any subjective patient interviews

explanation: Validating helps you catch mix-ups or misunderstandings early, so you don't build a care plan on the wrong information. Always good to double-check!

question: What is the main difference between a wound dressing and a bandage?

options.A: A dressing is only for bone fractures, and bandages are for skin cuts.
options.B: A bandage absorbs drainage, while a dressing provides structural support.
options.C: A bandage is always sterile, whereas dressings are never sterile.
options.D: A dressing touches the wound directly, while a bandage holds the dressing in place.

explanation: Think of it this way: the dressing is the sweet layer right on the open skin soaking up fluids, while the bandage wraps around it to keep everything secure. You've got this!

question: An administrator says 'no' to your staffing proposal because it costs too much. What is your best next move?

options.A: Organize a violent protest outside the administrative office
options.B: Prepare constructive evidence showing long-term cost savings and safety
options.C: Threaten the administrator with a media boycott
options.D: Abandon the advocacy campaign immediately and give up

explanation: Smart thinking! Coming back with solid proof that your idea improves safety and saves money in the long run is way more effective than getting upset.

question: During transport, who is mainly responsible for checking vital signs and giving medications?

options.A: The dispatcher
options.B: The mechanic
options.C: The pilot
options.D: The nurse

explanation: That's you! As the transport nurse, your main focus is keeping a close eye on the patient, managing fluids, and delivering medications right when they're needed.

question: What is the main thing a nurse does when acting as a health advocate?

options.A: Diagnosing complex medical conditions independently
options.B: Prescribing emergency medications during shortages
options.C: Speaking up for patients and protecting their rights
options.D: Managing the financial budget of the health facility

explanation: You got this! Being a health advocate simply means standing up for your patients, defending their rights, and helping them navigate the healthcare system.

question: Where do the best nursing research ideas usually spark from?

options.A: Everyday clinical observations
options.B: Hospital financial statements
options.C: Government tax reports
options.D: Pharmaceutical marketing brochures

explanation: Think about things you notice right on the ward! The challenges and patterns you see during clinical rotations make the most meaningful research topics.

question: When an endocrine gland responds to 'humoral' stimulation, what is it actually reacting to?

options.A: Direct commands from the cerebral cortex
options.B: Levels of nutrients and ions in the blood
options.C: Electrical signals from the spinal cord
options.D: The presence of circulating releasing factors

explanation: Great job remembering this! 'Humoral' just means the gland is tasting the blood for things like calcium or glucose and reacting to what it finds.

question: What is the main difference between a normal fear and a phobia?

options.A: A phobia only happens during sleep
options.B: A normal fear never causes physical symptoms
options.C: A normal fear lasts for many years
options.D: A phobia is out of proportion to any actual danger

explanation: Phobias involve an extreme and irrational reaction that does not match the real level of threat present. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h1)

question: You are putting AED pads on a man with a very hairy chest, and the pads won't stick well. What should you do right away?

options.A: Press the pads down firmly over the thick hair anyway
options.B: Skip using the AED and rely entirely on chest compressions
options.C: Apply conductive ultrasound gel over the dry hair first
options.D: Shave the hair quickly using a razor from the AED kit

explanation: Hair creates air pockets that block the electrical current. Luckily, AED kits come with a handy little razor so you can do a quick dry shave and get a solid stick!

question: What is the main rule of triage when a massive accident brings in dozens of injured people at once?

options.A: Sending all patients with minor injuries home immediately
options.B: Ensuring every patient is seen by a doctor within five minutes
options.C: Treating the most severely injured patient first regardless of outcome
options.D: Doing the greatest good for the greatest number of people

explanation: You nailed it! In mass casualties, resources are limited, so we focus on saving as many lives as we possibly can.

question: What is a common physical change that happens to the prostate gland as men age?

options.A: Total loss of the ability to produce seminal fluid
options.B: Complete shrinkage of the glandular tissue
options.C: Development of chronic bacterial infections in all men
options.D: Gradual enlargement that can affect urinary flow

explanation: You got it! The prostate tends to grow larger with age, which can sometimes press against the urethra and make urinating a bit tricky.

question: A nurse in a clinic after a severe flood is busy checking water supplies and looking out for skin rashes. What phase of disaster care is this?

options.A: Pre-disaster planning
options.B: Emergency architectural damage assessment
options.C: Recovery and stopping secondary disease outbreaks
options.D: Immediate search and rescue operations

explanation: Watching water and skin health after a flood helps catch and stop fresh infections while the community heals. Brilliant work today!

question: Why do nurses wear masks in the hospital?

options.A: To keep warm in air-conditioned rooms
options.B: To prevent patients from seeing the nurse's facial expressions
options.C: To eliminate the need for hand washing
options.D: To stop airborne and droplet germs from spreading

explanation: Masks act as a shield to keep harmful germs from traveling through the air between patients and staff. You've got this!

question: A nurse carefully documents every single dressing change and item used on a patient's chart. How does this affect hospital financing?

options.A: It automatically increases the national tax rate for citizens
options.B: It forces the government to stop using donor funds
options.C: It guarantees the patient will be discharged the same day
options.D: It ensures accurate billing and prevents loss of facility revenue

explanation: Good documentation means the hospital accurately accounts for every service given, ensuring proper insurance reimbursement and keeping the clinic funded to help the next patient.

question: Which service helps a person with a physical disability return to productive work matching their current functional level?

options.A: Emergency surgical services
options.B: Vocational rehabilitation
options.C: Acute hospital triage
options.D: Palliative hospice care

explanation: Vocational rehabilitation programs assess remaining skills and train individuals for new jobs suited to their physical abilities. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h7)

question: A unit manager in a busy Nigerian hospital wants to boost staff morale and reduce burnout. Which leadership approach should they lean on?

options.A: Purely autocratic and punitive management
options.B: Strictly laissez-faire indifference
options.C: Transformational and servant leadership
options.D: Exclusive reliance on physical punishment

explanation: To tackle burnout and keep spirits high, leaders need to empower, mentor, and care for their staff using transformational and servant styles.

question: Why is the HbA1c test so helpful for managing diabetes over time?

options.A: It detects acute kidney failure caused by high blood sugar spikes
options.B: It measures the exact amount of insulin stored inside pancreatic beta cells
options.C: It evaluates the immediate effect of the patient's last meal on glucose
options.D: It shows average blood sugar levels over the past two to three months

explanation: Spot on! Because sugar binds to red blood cells for their whole lifespan, HbA1c gives us a reliable historical report card of blood sugar over 2 to 3 months.

question: What special shape helps red blood cells squeeze through tiny blood vessels and carry plenty of oxygen?

options.A: Biconcave disc shape
options.B: Spherical amoeboid form
options.C: Rod-like crystalline structure
options.D: Presence of multiple nuclei

explanation: You nailed it! Their unique biconcave shape (flattened donuts without holes) gives them a massive surface area and makes them super flexible to squeeze through tight spots.

question: What is the main purpose of an Information Retrieval System in nursing?

options.A: To write nursing care plans without human input
options.B: To store, organize, and quickly find relevant clinical data
options.C: To automatically diagnose complex patient illnesses
options.D: To track daily hospital staff attendance records

explanation: An IRS is built specifically to help users locate stored information like research papers and clinical guidelines out of massive databases. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the big difference between a totally blame-free environment and a 'Just Culture'?

options.A: A blame-free environment punishes all errors severely
options.B: A blame-free environment requires police involvement for slips
options.C: A Just Culture ignores minor mistakes made by doctors
options.D: A Just Culture still holds workers accountable for reckless actions

explanation: Remember, 'Just Culture' isn't a free-for-all. We forgive honest human slips, but we draw a hard line against dangerous, reckless shortcuts.

question: How does having a daily work schedule help a client dealing with auditory hallucinations?

options.A: It replaces the need for any psychiatric evaluation
options.B: It blocks all sound waves from entering the ears
options.C: It completely cures the brain of abnormal electrical impulses
options.D: It provides a healthy distraction from distressing symptoms

explanation: When clients are busy focusing on work tasks, they have less time to dwell on troubling internal voices. You're doing great!

question: What is the main way the heart automatically matches its blood supply to its workload?

options.A: Opening of heart valves during systole
options.B: Control by the kidneys via blood pressure
options.C: Local metabolic autoregulation
options.D: Direct command from the cerebral cortex

explanation: Correct! The heart uses smart local chemical changes in its own tissue to automatically adjust vessel size and keep the blood flowing where it's needed most.

question: How do we classify used surgical blades and needles in the hospital?

options.A: General waste
options.B: Pathological waste
options.C: Sharps
options.D: Pharmaceutical waste

explanation: Great job! Any tool that can cut or puncture the skin, like needles and blades, is known specifically as a sharp.

question: What do we call it when a hospital ward slowly slips back into old, messy habits after an improvement project finishes?

options.A: Systemic clinical drift
options.B: Relapse to old ways
options.C: Forcing function failure
options.D: Special cause variation

explanation: It's easy to slide back into comfort zones! That's why keeping new habits alive requires ongoing teamwork and support.

question: Why do teenagers often take big risks even when they know it's dangerous?

options.A: They experience a permanent loss of short-term memory
options.B: They completely lack the ability to think logically
options.C: Their cognitive development stops entirely during puberty
options.D: Reward-seeking brain centers develop faster than impulse-control centers

explanation: The thrill-seeking part of the brain develops faster than the brake pedal (impulse control), making exciting experiences feel totally worth the risk to them.

question: A patient on combined pills reports mild nausea and tender breasts during her first week. What should you tell her?

options.A: Recommend immediate emergency surgery to check for blood clots
options.B: Reassure her that these are common mild adjustment side effects
options.C: Tell her to double her daily dose to help her body adjust faster
options.D: Instruct her to stop taking all medication immediately and report to the doctor

explanation: Take a breath—minor side effects are totally normal when starting estrogen as the body gets used to the new hormone levels. They usually clear up after a cycle or two!

question: What is the main goal of teaching 'pacing' to a patient with fatigue?

options.A: To replace physical movement entirely with mental relaxation
options.B: To complete all daily chores twice as fast as before
options.C: To eliminate the need for any sleep during the night
options.D: To prevent total energy depletion by taking breaks before exhaustion hits

explanation: Brilliant! Pacing is all about working smarter, not harder. By resting *before* running completely out of gas, patients avoid crashing for days afterward.

question: When planning community-based rehabilitation, why do we use local materials?

options.A: To ban all physical tools during therapy sessions
options.B: To rely completely on single-use plastics
options.C: To require buying advanced technology from abroad
options.D: To encourage using low-cost, locally available items

explanation: Correct! Sustainable care uses things people can easily find, afford, and fix right in their own neighborhoods without breaking the bank.

question: Is the pH of normal semen acidic, neutral, or alkaline?

options.A: Slightly acidic
options.B: Extremely acidic
options.C: Alkaline
options.D: Neutral

explanation: Semen is alkaline, which acts like a protective shield against the naturally acidic environment inside the female reproductive tract.

question: A nursing lecturer uses a physical heart model to explain blood flow to students with different learning styles. Which group benefits most from handling and examining this model directly?

options.A: Auditory learners
options.B: Kinesthetic learners
options.C: Visual learners
options.D: Reading learners

explanation: Kinesthetic learners learn best by touching, moving, and interacting physically with materials and models during a demonstration. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h2)

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of tele-nursing for patients?

options.A: Automatic provision of free smartphones to every citizen
options.B: Reduced travel time and lower transportation expenses
options.C: Guaranteed complete cure for all chronic illnesses
options.D: Elimination of all hospital fees and medicine costs

explanation: Exactly! Tele-nursing saves patients the stress, time, and money of traveling long distances just for routine check-ins or quick advice.

question: What is an obsession in someone dealing with obsessive-compulsive neurosis?

options.A: A physical movement done to relieve muscle tension
options.B: An intrusive and unwanted thought that causes anxiety
options.C: A sudden memory loss regarding personal identity
options.D: A complete loss of contact with external reality

explanation: Spot on! Think of an obsession as an unwelcome thought or image that keeps popping into the mind against the person's will, bringing along a lot of stress.

question: Why is it super important to check the publication date of an article before using it for clinical care?

options.A: Patients refuse to answer questions about outdated medical research
options.B: Publishers charge higher fees for journals printed in the current year
options.C: Clinical guidelines and best practices change rapidly as new research emerges
options.D: Older articles are always written by students rather than doctors

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare changes fast. Using old research might mean you are practicing outdated, unsafe nursing care.

question: Why are patients who suffer massive insect stings at risk for sudden kidney injury?

options.A: Profound low blood pressure and direct venom toxicity compromise renal perfusion
options.B: Patients refuse to drink water due to fear of swallowing
options.C: Venom causes direct physical blockage of the ureters by crystals
options.D: The kidneys work overtime to filter out oral antihistamine pills

explanation: Spot on! Severe shock starves the kidneys of blood flow, and heavy venom toxins can directly damage the delicate kidney tubules.

question: What is the main purpose of placing electrode pads on a patient's chest for cardiac monitoring?

options.A: To capture the electrical activity and heart rhythm
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient warm during cold hospital nights
options.D: To deliver mild electric shocks to warm the skin

explanation: Electrodes pick up the heart's electrical impulses and display them as a waveform on the screen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason for excluding a child from a nursery temporarily?

options.A: Persistent vomiting or unexplained severe diarrhea
options.B: A mild, clear runny nose without any fever or lethargy
options.C: An undiagnosed, contagious vesicular skin rash
options.D: A high fever accompanied by unusual lethargy

explanation: Mild upper respiratory symptoms like a clear runny nose without fever do not typically require exclusion, whereas contagious rashes, vomiting, and high fevers do. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h5)

question: Which neurological condition can be managed using anticholinergics to help reduce tremors?

options.A: Epilepsy
options.B: Multiple sclerosis
options.C: Alzheimer's disease
options.D: Parkinson's disease

explanation: Anticholinergics help balance neurotransmitters in the brain to control tremors in early Parkinson's disease. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T6#GNS223_U5_T6_h4)

question: During a quick check right after birth, which sign tells you the newborn is doing great?

options.A: Meconium present in the amniotic fluid
options.B: A slow and irregular breathing pattern
options.C: Pale skin and limp extremities
options.D: Good muscle tone and crying

explanation: A baby who cries loudly, moves their arms and legs, and has good muscle tone is telling you their brain and lungs are working wonderfully!

question: Why do negative feedback loops usually fail when a gland is overproducing hormones?

options.A: Target tissues stop responding to every chemical signal
options.B: The liver destroys the negative feedback receptors
options.C: The gland keeps releasing hormones despite high blood levels
options.D: The kidneys filter out all circulating hormones too fast

explanation: Normally, high hormone levels tell the body to slow down production. But in hypersecretion, this built-in brake system stops working properly and the gland just keeps pumping it out. Great job working through this concept! [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h1)

question: About what percentage of total waste generated in a hospital is typically non-hazardous?

options.A: Zero percent
options.B: 75 to 90 percent
options.C: 10 to 25 percent
options.D: 40 to 50 percent

explanation: That's right! The vast majority of hospital refuse is actually general domestic-type waste that doesn't pose biological hazards. Keep it up!

question: There is a sudden water shortage at the clinic, so you quickly improvise a clean handwashing station before dressing a wound. What are you doing here?

options.A: Practicing a fully compensatory self-care deficit model
options.B: Ignoring standard nursing care procedures entirely
options.C: Failing to follow strict hospital administration rules
options.D: Controlling the environment to prevent infection

explanation: Brilliant improvising! Finding a way to maintain cleanliness even when infrastructure fails is the true spirit of environmental control and safe nursing.

question: What is the main purpose of priority setting in community mobilisation?

options.A: To make sure every single disease is treated on day one
options.B: To delay health interventions until funding runs out
options.C: To let health workers choose projects without community input
options.D: To focus resources on the most urgent health problem first

explanation: Since resources are limited, ranking problems helps the community tackle the most critical issue first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h5)

question: Besides sharing new rules, what must effective communication include during a healthcare transition?

options.A: An explanation of why the change improves patient outcomes
options.B: Strict orders that forbid nurses from asking questions
options.C: Detailed financial records of the hospital budget
options.D: Immediate disciplinary threats for non-compliant staff members

explanation: When nurses see the 'why'—especially how it helps patients—they are much more willing to get on board.

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take when managing an active adverse drug reaction?

options.A: Discharging the patient home for proper rest
options.B: Calling the pharmaceutical manufacturing company
options.C: Starting broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately
options.D: Stopping the administration of the suspected drug

explanation: You've got this! Removing the source of the trouble is always the immediate step to protect your patient from further harm.
